narrative: The model estimates a 61% chance that you will leave, so leaving is judged more likely than staying; under the promotion rule, that prediction is why you are denied. The strongest factor is your overall work experience of one to five years, which pushes toward staying. This is a common profile, since about half of employees predicted to stay have the same range. The next most important factor is that you have other job opportunities while in this role, which pushes toward leaving. This stands out because most employees predicted to stay—about three in four—had no such opportunities. Your time in the current organization, also one to five years, is the third factor and slightly pushes toward leaving, although this range is likewise common among employees predicted to stay. Together, the pull of outside opportunities and current tenure outweigh the stabilizing signal of your overall experience, producing the 61% leave estimate. Before promotion can be reconsidered, it would be sensible to discuss what outside opportunities are attractive, whether growth, recognition, support and job satisfaction can be improved here, and whether you intend to stay. You may also want to clarify your career path and ask what would make remaining and advancing in this organization more compelling.
